topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how germline-encoded receptors distinguish signs of infection or damage from normal host components.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor pathways and inflammatory signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the receptor mechanisms that translate microbial or damage signals into inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated sentinel cells initiate inflammation that brings circulating immune cells to the infection site.

topics.label: Lymphatic transport and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how infection information leaves the tissue through lymphatic drainage to initiate adaptive responses in lymph nodes.

topics.label: Excessive systemic inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how excessive inflammatory activation becomes a life-threatening systemic response.

topics.label: Mechanisms of inflammation resolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the balance of inflammatory activation and inhibition shifts to shut down an immune response.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what happens when damaged tissue cannot be fully restored to an inflammation-free state, including containment of persistent infection.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and identifies complement as the subject of the next lecture.
